newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish finmin says grain duties bad for inflation.
newsitem.headline: Polish finmin says grain duties bad for inflation.

text.p: Polish Finance Minister Grzegorz Kolodko criticised the cabinet's decision on Tuesday to reinstate duties on grain imports, saying the move could upset this year's inflation goals.

"With great regret I accept the government decision on partial reintroduction of duties on grains, I was the only one to vote against this decision," Kolodko told a news briefing after the government meeting.
The government decided to introduce duties on most grains, originally suspended until mid-1997 but also decided to halve the duties to 10 percent from earlier 20 percent.
"Because of this decision the annual average 15-percent inflation goal (for 1997)...is seriously threatened. It is regrettable that the government gave in to political arguments," Kolodko said.
The introduction of grain imports duty ahead of schedule was advocated by Agriculture Minister Roman Jagielinski and his co-ruling Polish Peasant Party (PSL).

Jagielinski has argued that duty-free grains imports, introducted in the first half of 1996 when grain prices were mounting, should now end because the market has stabilised after substantial imports and good grains output prospects.

But opposition politicians and some analysts said the PSL wants to reinstate the duty to protect interest of the electorate, mostly rural, ahead of this year's parliamentary elections. -- Warsaw Newsroom +48 22 653 9700
